extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying functional analysis (Banach and Hilbert spaces)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of classical properties and results about sequence spaces (ℓ^p, c, c0, ℓ^∞), duals, reflexivity, separability, and differences/analogues when the base field is C; plus standard Hilbert-space results (Riesz representation, projection theorem, spectrum, numerical range, Lax–Milgram).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of c and c0
rubrics_metrics.description: c = {x; lim_{k→∞} x_k exists}, c0 = {x; lim_{k→∞} x_k = 0}. Both equipped with the ℓ^∞ norm; c0 ⊂ c ⊂ ℓ^∞ and c0 closed in c, c closed in ℓ^∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to contrast separability and dual-space descriptions later; explicit identification of limits and inclusions is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hölder's inequality (sequence form)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p, q ≤ ∞ with 1/p + 1/q = 1, ∑_{k=1}^∞ x_k y_k ≤ ||x||_p ||y||_q for x ∈ ℓ^p, y ∈ ℓ^q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as the basic inequality used to identify dual pairings and for norm estimates throughout proofs (e.g., bounding φ(x)=∑ u_k x_k).

rubrics_metrics.name: ℓ^2 is a Hilbert space
rubrics_metrics.description: ℓ^2 is a Hilbert space equipped with the scalar product (x,y) = ∑_{k=1}^∞ x_k y_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets up using standard inner product structure and later Riesz-representation-type arguments in ℓ^2 contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusions and norm inequalities among ℓ^p spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p < ∞, ℓ^p ⊂ c0 and ||x||_∞ ≤ ||x||_p. If 1 ≤ p ≤ q ≤ ∞ then ℓ^p ⊂ ℓ^q and ||x||_q ≤ ||x||_p for x ∈ ℓ^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inequalities give the chain of inclusions used to compare spaces and to deduce properties (e.g., separability, reflexivity) across p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 11.15: Reflexivity and uniform convexity of ℓ^p (1<p<∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: The space ℓ^p is reflexive, and even uniformly convex, for 1 < p < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reference: apply general results (Theorem 4.10 and Exercise 4.12) with the counting measure on N; used to justify reflexivity of these classical sequence spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 11.16: Separability of c, c0, and ℓ^p (1≤p<∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spaces c, c0, and ℓ^p (1 ≤ p < ∞) are separable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit countable dense set D = sequences with rational coordinates and finite support; for c add D + λ(1,1,1,...) with λ∈Q to be dense in c.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 11.17: Nonseparability of ℓ^∞
rubrics_metrics.description: The space ℓ^∞ is not separable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a sequence b differing by at least 1 from each element of any given countable set A ⊂ ℓ^∞ (diagonal-type construction) to show no countable set can be dense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual of ℓ^p (1≤p<∞) identification (Proposition 11.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p < ∞, every φ ∈ (ℓ^p)* is represented uniquely by some u ∈ ℓ^q (1/p + 1/q = 1) such that φ(x) = ∑_{k=1}^∞ u_k x_k for all x ∈ ℓ^p, and ||u||_q = ||φ||_{(ℓ^p)*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs u_k = φ(e_k) and uses Hölder and appropriate test sequences to show u ∈ ℓ^q and equality of norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual of c0 is ℓ^1 (Proposition 11.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any φ ∈ (c0)* there exists a unique u ∈ ℓ^1 such that φ(x) = ∑_{k=1}^∞ u_k x_k ∀x ∈ c0, and ||u||_1 = ||φ||_{(c0)*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adaptation of ℓ^p duality with p=∞, q=1; uses density of finitely supported sequences in c0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual of c is ℓ^1 × R (Proposition 11.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For φ ∈ c*, there exists a unique pair (u,λ) ∈ ℓ^1 × R with φ(x) = ∑_{k=1}^∞ u_k x_k + λ lim_{k→∞} x_k ∀x ∈ c, and ||u||_1 + |λ| = ||φ||_{c*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decompose x ∈ c as y + a e where y∈c0 and a = lim x_k; apply dual of c0 to φ|_{c0} and compute λ = φ(e) − ∑ u_k. Norm equality shown by suitable test sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-reflexivity of ℓ^1, ℓ^∞, c, c0 (Proposition 11.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spaces ℓ^1, ℓ^∞, c, and c0 are not reflexive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identifications of duals from previous propositions and the canonical injection not being surjective; also closed-subspace arguments (if c were reflexive then c0, as closed subspace, would be reflexive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification between complex and real duals (Proposition 11.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: The map I: f ↦ Re f is a bijective isometry from the complex dual E* onto the real dual E*_R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how complex duals relate to real duals via real-part mapping; includes constructive inverse f(x)=ϕ(x) − iϕ(ix) for ϕ ∈ E*_R and norm estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hahn–Banach extension over C preserving norm (Proposition 11.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If g is a continuous linear functional on a linear subspace G ⊂ E (over C), then there exists f ∈ E* extending g with ||f||_{E*} = ||g||_{G*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to real-case extension via Re g and then uses Proposition 11.22 to lift back to complex functional preserving norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric form of Hahn–Banach in complex spaces (Proposition 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given disjoint nonempty convex A, B ⊂ E with one open, there exists a closed real hyperplane H = {x; Re⟨f,x⟩ = α} that separates A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation is by a 'real' hyperplane (Re f) rather than a complex-linear hyperplane; uses real Hahn–Banach and Proposition 11.23 to lift to complex functionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fenchel–Moreau biconjugation for complex vector spaces (Proposition 11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ: E → (−∞,+∞] is convex, l.s.c., and not identically +∞, then ϕ^{**} = ϕ (biconjugate equals function).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either apply real result to ER or repeat proof using real hyperplane separation; conjugate defined using Re⟨f,x⟩.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonal complement and double orthogonal identity
rubrics_metrics.description: For a linear subspace M ⊂ E, M^⊥ = {f ∈ E*; ⟨f,x⟩=0 ∀x∈M}, and M^{⊥⊥} = M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard dual-space orthogonality notion holds in complex spaces (Re may be used in definition equally well).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic properties of complex Hilbert spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: A Hilbert space over C has scalar product (u,v) ∈ C satisfying conjugate symmetry, linearity in the first argument, positivity; induced norm |u|=(u,u)^{1/2}, parallelogram-type identity and Cauchy–Schwarz |(u,v)| ≤ |u||v|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes connection with real Hilbert space HR via Re(u,v) and applicability of real results to complex case; L^2((Ω);C) example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection theorem in Hilbert space (Proposition 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K ⊂ H is nonempty closed convex, then for every f ∈ H there exists a unique u ∈ K minimizing |f − v| over v∈K; u characterized by u∈K and Re(f−u,v−u) ≤ 0 ∀v∈K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard nearest-point projection with variational characterization via real part of inner products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riesz representation in complex Hilbert space (Proposition 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any continuous linear functional ϕ ∈ H* there exists a unique f ∈ H with ϕ(u) = (u,f) ∀u∈H and ||f|| = ||ϕ||_{H*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof applies the real Riesz to Re ϕ on HR and recovers imaginary part via iu; standard identification used throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lax–Milgram style results and coercivity conditions (Propositions 11.28 and 11.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a(u,v) is bilinear (linear in each variable), continuous |a(u,v)| ≤ C|u||v|, and coercive Re a(u,u) ≥ α|u|^2 (α>0), then for any ϕ∈H* there exists unique u∈K solving Re a(u,v−u) ≥ Re⟨ϕ,v−u⟩ ∀v∈K. In particular if K=H, a(u,v) = ⟨ϕ,v⟩ has a unique solution; operators T with Re(Tu,u) ≥ α|u|^2 are bijective. A weaker-looking condition |(Tu,u)| ≥ α|u|^2 also implies bijectivity (Lax–Milgram variant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives variational existence/uniqueness and bijectivity of coercive operators; remarks connect (17) ⇒ (18) and show how to rotate in complex plane to obtain coercivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum properties for operators on complex Banach spaces (Proposition 11.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: For T∈L(E) with E over C, the spectrum σ(T) is a nonempty compact set and σ(T) ⊂ {λ∈C; |λ| ≤ ||T||}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonemptiness relies on complex-analytic arguments (Liouville); includes mention that bound |λ| ≤ ||T|| is usually not sharp and spectral radius gives better estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral radius identity (Proposition 11.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every T∈L(E), r(T) = lim_{n→∞} ||T^n||^{1/n} exists and equals max{|λ|; λ ∈ σ(T)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses complex analysis tools; equality may fail over R in the same strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral mapping theorem for polynomials in complex case (Proposition 11.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q(t) is a polynomial with complex coefficients and T∈L(E) over C, then Q(EV(T)) = EV(Q(T)) and Q(σ(T)) = σ(Q(T)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In complex case the inclusions become equalities; proof uses factorization Q(t)−μ=α∏(t−t_i) and algebraic arguments about bijectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical range W(T): containment, resolvent bound, and convexity (Proposition 11.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: For T∈L(H) on a complex Hilbert space, σ(T) ⊂ W(T) where W(T) = {(Tu,u); |u|=1}. If λ∉W(T) then λ∈ρ(T) and ||(T−λI)^{-1}|| ≤ 1/dist(λ,W(T)). Moreover W(T) is convex (Toeplitz–Hausdorff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Lax–Milgram to show invertibility outside W(T) and the bound on resolvent; convexity is a classical but nontrivial fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoint conventions in complex Hilbert spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Two viewpoints: the adjoint T* as map on H* and as operator on H (via Riesz identification) coincide up to conjugation behavior: (λT)* = barλ T* (equation (24)) i.e. scalar multiples conjugate when passed to adjoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important sign/conjugation convention: T* behaves conjugate-linearly with respect to scalar multiplication in the usual operator-on-H identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-adjoint operators and real spectrum/numerical range
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is self-adjoint (T* = T), then (Tu,u) ∈ R ∀u, so W(T) ⊂ R and hence σ(T) ⊂ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate corollary of self-adjointness and numerical-range containment of spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral decomposition for compact self-adjoint operators (Proposition 11.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: If H is separable and T is compact self-adjoint, then there exists a Hilbert basis composed of eigenvectors of T and the corresponding eigenvalues are real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same as real-case theorem but emphasizes eigenvalues are real in the self-adjoint complex case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal operators: norm equals spectral radius (Proposition 11.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is normal (T* T = T T*), then max{|λ|; λ∈σ(T)} = ||T||.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses ||T^p|| = ||T||^p for integers p≥1 and relates r(T) to ||T||; relies on normality and earlier spectral radius identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact normal operator eigenbasis (Proposition 11.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: If H is separable and T is compact normal, there exists a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors of T; eigenvalues need not be real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orthogonality of eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues and reduction to finite-dimensional spectral arguments are used; complex field is essential for some steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical range equals convex hull of spectrum for normal operators (Remark 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For normal T (in particular compact normal), W(T) = conv σ(T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated using eigenbasis expansion when T is compact normal; more generally holds for normal operators (references given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum of isometries and unitaries (Proposition 11.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is an isometry then EV(T) ⊂ S^1 = {λ∈C; |λ|=1}. If T is unitary then σ(T) ⊂ S^1. If T is an isometry but not unitary then σ(T) = {λ∈C; |λ| ≤ 1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows by adapting real-space arguments; includes distinction between isometry and unitary (surjectivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skew-adjoint (antisymmetric) operators spectrum location
rubrics_metrics.description: If T* = −T (skew-adjoint), then iT is self-adjoint and hence EV(T) ⊂ σ(T) ⊂ W(T) ⊂ iR (spectrum contained on imaginary axis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from relation to self-adjointness via multiplication by i and the numerical-range/spectrum containment facts.
